# Exotic Customer Table

*Page PDF 23*

## **Exotic Customer Table**
Roll 1d10. If the tavern is a Silver Tier location, add 5 to the roll. If it is a Gold Tier location, add 10 to the roll. 

| d10 | Exotic Guests |
|---|---|
| 1–2 | Folk from a distant land. This group of four may be a family or a group of fellow travellers. . They know little of the local language and customs and tend to keep to themselves.  Difficult (–10) Gossip A chatty individual who quickly turns conversation to a controversial belief, such as |
| 3 | Lurid Conspiracy Theorist. local rulers being Vampires, or that a local business provides cover to criminals.  Very Easy (+60) Gossip . Pedlars. |
| 4 | Group of three Strigany Pedlars with several wicker baskets containing pegs, pins, and cutlery. They keep to themselves unless approached by someone interested in their wares.  Hard (–20) Gossip . Confectionary Seller.  An elderly man who walks about the bar with a box of slightly stale sweetmeats. He sells a 5 sweet for a penny.  Easy (+40) Gossip  but grows offended if a guest does not buy a sweet following a conversation. Meat Auction. |
| 6 | A local pair who work in a slaughterhouse. They have cuts of beef or mutton that they are willing to sell for 2d per steak.  Challenging (+0) Gossip . |
| 7–8 | Off the Beat.  An off-duty watch patrol of four men. Depending on the mien of the other customers, they may either be garrulous and talkative ( Easy (+40) Gossip ) or rather subdued ( Hard (–20) Gossip ). Mootland Wine Merchant.  A Halfling Trader with a keg of Whistler’s Finest Rose Wine. She is offering glasses of it to anyone who fancies a taste. She is hoping that she can generate enough enthusiasm for the wine that the 9 landlord will agree to stock it.  Easy (+40) Gossip , but if she is seen passing out more than one glass to a particular guest, the landlord becomes angry with everyone involved. Missionaries. |
| 10 | A pair of Shallyan Nuns. They warn folk of the dangers of drink and are stern and serious. Whilst the landlord resents them being here, he is too afraid of causing a backlash by barring them.  Hard (–20) Gossip . Healer.  A Physician with a Heal Skill of 30+3d10, the  Surgery  Talent, and a medical kit containing bandages, 11 poultices, and herbal remedies.  Average (+20) Gossip . Sigmarite Priest.  A Priest of Sigmar with the  Bless  and  Invoke |
| 12–13 | Talents, and a Pray Skill of 35+4d10. They have the full complement of Sigmarite Blessings and Miracles from the  WFRP Core Rulebook .  Average (+20) Gossip . Licensed Wizard.  A Wizard from one of the colleges. They may have their familiar with them, and if so, this will |
| 14–15 | be the cause of significant consternation amongst other guests and bar staff. The Wizard’s college and abilities are left to the GM, but they should at least have the Channelling and Language (Magick) skills of 35+4d10, 4 Petty Spells, and 4 Lore Spells.  Challenging (+0) Gossip . Famous Face.  A celebrated Artist or cultural figure, such as a painter, playwright, sculptor, musician, architect, |
| 16 | Scholar, or philosopher. Characters with appropriate Lore Skills may have heard of the individual. They may well be travelling to take on a commission for a new patron and have a small entourage in tow.  Challenging (+0) Gossip . Legal Team.  A group of four Lawyers. They take a table in the corner and are engaged in a hushed discussion. They |
| 17 | may be dealing with the intricacies of a difficult case and will most likely be a team representing the same client. There is a chance that they are representing opposing clients and are conspiring to bring the trial to a particular conclusion.  Very Hard (–30) Gossip . Hunting Party.  A minor Noble or wealthy Merchant on a hunting expedition (if near the country) or visit from a |
| 18–19 | neighbouring province (if not). They have a dozen friends and Servants with them, including well-armed Guards. If hunting, they have hounds and horses with them, and the stables are probably at capacity.  Hard (–20) Gossip . Regal Progress.  A senior member of an important noble family and their entourage. This may even be a noble household going about on progress. The number of Servants, Guards, and attachés is so large that they will likely |
| 20 | command every room in the inn, and most of the seats in the taproom. The staff of the inn will be utterly devoted to providing all their attention to this individual and their senior servants and may even ask other customers to quit the premises altogether.  Very Hard (–30) Gossip . |
